rationale: Switch the features from the referential montage to the 18-channel bipolar double-banana montage. Referential signals share the reference electrode's activity, which blurs focal, low-amplitude neonatal seizures across all channels. Bipolar derivations cancel that shared activity and keep the local rhythmic discharges, so max-over-channel features should separate seizure from background better. Everything else is unchanged so this round isolates the montage effect.

I'm changing the preprocessing to the clinical neonatal pipeline: re-reference to the 18-channel bipolar double-banana montage and band-pass filter at 0.5–30 Hz before computing the same features. In the referential montage, activity at the common reference and slow drift or high-frequency artefacts swamp the low-amplitude focal rhythmic discharges, so the per-channel maximum may not pick them out. Bipolar derivations localize those discharges, and the filter stops noise from inflating line length and RMS. This is untested; the harness will show whether it beats the current 0.7587.

I'm replacing the 19 referential channels with the standard 18-channel neonatal double-banana bipolar montage. In a referential montage the shared reference electrode adds the same activity and artifacts to every channel, which hides seizures that are focal, low-amplitude and confined to one region. Bipolar derivations cancel that shared signal and show local rhythmic discharges, and this is the montage clinical annotators read. The features, classifier and smoothing stay the same, so any change in the Dev score comes from the montage alone.

All features, the classifier and the smoothing stay the same.

The current features come from referential signals that share a reference, which hides focal low-amplitude seizures and lets drift and noise dominate. This version first band-pass filters each recording at 0.5–30 Hz, then converts it to the 18-channel bipolar double-banana montage used clinically and by Tapani et al. Per-channel features and max/median across channels are then computed on those bipolar derivations. The classifier and smoothing are unchanged. I haven't run it, so there is no Dev score for this version yet.

Neonatal seizures are focal. With the referential montage, the shared reference picks up widespread activity and artifacts that mask local rhythmic discharges. This change derives the 18-channel neonatal bipolar double-banana montage and band-passes it at 0.5–30 Hz (removing drift, mains noise and EMG) before computing the same features. Local seizure activity should then be much more visible in the max-over-channels features.
